subject: Policy scope selector + on-demand erasures: roadmap & mutual action plan
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@halcyonhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant-level erasure & regional storage options (initial ask)

Hi Soojin,

We are evaluating Redwood for a multi-tenant deployment and have two tightly coupled compliance asks that are blockers for our security/infosec review:

1) Tenant-scoped retention policies that an admin can configure per-workspace (we need presets + ability to create custom TTLs). This must include an API so we can automate initial provisioning.

2) On-demand erasure: when a record/tenant requests deletion, we need a documented erase flow that guarantees data is removed from storage and backups, plus an auditable confirmation delivered within 72 hours. For regulated datasets, we also need region-bound storage (US-only) and a way to pin a tenant to a specific storage region.

Can you share how Redwood plans to support these features (API + UI + timeline)? Also — any constraints around KMS/key separation and where audit logs for erasures will live would be helpful.

We'd like a short mutual action plan if this is doable. Attaching a basic matrix of our expectations.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Senior Security Program Manager
Halcyon Health

Team — forwarding Halcyon's request. High-level asks: per-tenant TTL presets + custom TTL, API + admin UI, on-demand erasure with auditable confirmation (<72h), and ability to pin tenants to US-only storage. They also ask about KMS separation and where erasure/audit logs live.

Can engineering and product weigh in on feasibility and propose a short MAP (mutual action plan) and rough ETA for an MVP? Key product questions to answer:
- Should we model retention as a tenant config (single row) or as a per-resource policy?
- Erasure semantics: soft-delete + background purge vs immediate crypto-shred?
- Backups: do we need an explicit backup-retention/override?
- Admin UI + API surface and expected endpoints.

I attached a quick retention presets matrix and a draft SLA note. I think a 3-sprint MVP might be plausible but need engineering estimates.

Thanks — Soojin

Subject: Re: Fwd: Tenant-level erasure & regional storage options (initial ask)

Thanks for the flag — quick technical notes: we can support this but there are tradeoffs. High-level approach I recommend:

- Tenant-config object in the config service with fields: retention_policy_id, residency_region, legal_hold_flag, last_erase_request_id. This keeps evaluation cheap at request time and avoids per-object metadata bloat.
- Retention presets: implemented as named policy rows that the admin/UI can map to a tenant. Presets stored as policy definitions (TTL, soft-delete window, backup-exclude flag).
- Erasure semantics: MVP = soft-delete + queued purge worker that performs object-level purge from active stores and triggers backup-rotation markers; permanent purge from cold backups runs on a separate schedule. Crypto-shred (key deletion) is feasible only if tenant uses a dedicated CMEK (customer-managed key) and we can ensure key isolation.
- Regional storage: enforce at routing layer and ensure that blob placement is restricted to storage pools tagged by region. We'll need a migration plan for existing tenants.
- Audit trail: emit erasure events to the audit-log service (immutable stream), and include a signed erasure confirmation document generated by a job.

Estimated effort: discovery + design (1 sprint), schema & API (1 sprint), routing + storage enforcement + purge worker (1-2 sprints). MVP to pilot in 3 sprints with strong caveats around backups and cross-region restore paths.

Risks / open questions:
- Backup retention overlap: if backups are immutable for X days, we need policy to mark records for purge and coordinate backup retention windows.
- Legal hold complexity: we should allow an API to place/remove legal holds and block purge.
- Telemetry & SLA: erasure confirmation SLA will require instrumentation and retries; 72-hour target looks achievable for active stores but backups may stretch it unless we accelerate backup purge.

I'll draft a tech spec once product locks scope.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Tenant-level erasure & regional storage options (initial ask)

Agree with Karthik's approach. From a product/CS perspective we should propose the following in our MAP:

- Presets: 30d, 90d, 365d, indefinite + an option for custom days. Admin API and Console UI to select preset at tenant creation and change it later (with change audit).
- On-demand erasure: provide an API endpoint POST /v1/tenants/{id}/erasure-requests with optional force_full_purge flag (CMEK only). Provide an erasure confirmation document (PDF) with an event id and timestamp.
- Legal hold flow: separate boolean + admin reason + expiry metadata. Holds should block purge workers and surface in UI with blocking warnings.
- Regional pinning: expose residency_region on tenant create and a migration tool for existing tenants to request region pin (with manual approval).

Operational asks: we need runbook for incident scenarios, a telemetry dashboard to track outstanding erasure requests, and a playable playbook for audits showing proof of purges. Also requires sign-off from security on the audit artifact format.

Timeline ask to engineering: can we commit to a pilot (limited beta) by end of Q4 if we start discovery next week? If not, propose alternate scope for Q4 (API + audit events only).

-Marissa
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

Lena — thanks for the clear ask and for the matrix. Consolidating internal feedback into a short Mutual Action Plan below. Please let me know if you'd like this as a one-pager or a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Week 1 (2026-08-31): Discovery & scoping call (we'll confirm backup constraints and CMEK needs).
- Week 2 (2026-09-07): Design sprint + tech spec (product + infra owners).
- Sprint 1 (2026-09-14 to 2026-09-27): Implement tenant-config model + API endpoints + audit-event plumbing.
- Sprint 2 (2026-09-28 to 2026-10-11): Storage routing & residency enforcement, admin UI mocks integrated.
- Sprint 3 (2026-10-12 to 2026-10-25): Purge workers, backup coordination, erasure confirmation PDF generator; internal quality + compliance review.
- Pilot (target): start pilot with Halcyon Health in early November.

Deliverables for Halcyon to prepare: the list of tenant IDs that need US-only pinning; KMS/CMEK requirements per tenant (if applicable); examples of the types of data that must be purged vs. archived.

Open items / constraints:
- Backup purge timeline may extend erasure completion depending on existing retention. We'll surface exact guarantees after discovery.
- Crypto-shred option requires dedicated CMEK and will impact restore/business continuity; we'll document tradeoffs.
